1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False)``,
5	``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, costs=None, trace=False,
6	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False)``,
7	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
8	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False)`` and
9	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``.
10	
11	Semantics:
12	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
13	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
14	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
15	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
16	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
17	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
18	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
19	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
20	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
21	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
22	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
23	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
24	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
25	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
26	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
27	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
28	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
29	
30	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
31	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
32	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
33	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
34	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
35	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
36	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
37	  check) and before the search starts.
38	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
39	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
40	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
41	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
42	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
43	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
44	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
45	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
46	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
47	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
48	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
49	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
50	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
51	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
52	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
53	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
54	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
55	  accepts no budget parameter.
56	
57	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
58	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
59	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
60	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
61	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
62	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
63	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
64	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
65	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
66	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
67	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
68	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
69	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
70	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
71	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
72	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
73	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
74	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
75	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
76	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
77	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
78	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
79	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
80	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
81	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
82	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
83	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
84	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
85	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
86	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
87	
88	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
89	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
90	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
91	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
92	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
93	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
94	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
95	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
96	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
97	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
98	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
99	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
100	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
101	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
102	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
103	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
104	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
105	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
106	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
107	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
108	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
109	  other arrival times still compete.
110	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
111	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
112	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
113	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
114	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
115	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
116	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
117	  better route with a worse one.
118	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
119	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
120	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
121	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
122	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
123	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
124	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
125	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
126	  and step count.
127	
128	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
129	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
130	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
131	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
132	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
133	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
134	  included) and before the search starts.
135	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
136	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
137	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
138	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
139	  carry the field.
140	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
141	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
142	  candidate goals, costs and dynamic frames), the closed-node count, the
143	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
144	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
145	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
146	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
147	  back to ``resume`` later.
148	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
149	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
150	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
151	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
152	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
153	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
154	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
155	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
156	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
157	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
158	  closed node twice.
159	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
160	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
161	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
162	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
163	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
164	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
165	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
166	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
167	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
168	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
169	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
170	
171	Offline replay (``replay``):
172	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
173	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
174	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
175	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
176	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
177	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
178	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
179	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
180	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
181	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
182	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
183	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
184	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
185	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
186	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
187	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
188	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
189	  ``start == goal``.
190	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
191	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
192	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
193	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
194	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
195	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
196	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
197	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
198	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
199	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
200	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
201	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
202	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
203	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
204	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
205	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
206	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
207	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
208	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
209	  ever returned.
210	
211	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
212	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
213	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
214	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
215	  normalized to tuples.
216	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
217	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
218	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
219	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
220	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
221	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
222	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
223	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
224	"""

429	def _search_static(width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, trace,
430	                   max_expanded, snapshot=False, state=None):
431	    """Classic static-grid A* (the ``plan`` search without frames).
432	
433	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
434	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``
435	    reconstructs the cheapest route once the goal is closed. With
436	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
437	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
438	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs
439	    the trace even when the caller did not ask for it, so nodes are
440	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.
441	    """
442	
443	    def heuristic(point):
444	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
445	
446	    def step_cost(point):
447	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
448	        if costs is None:
449	            return 1
450	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
451	
452	    if state is None:
453	        # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, point): the first four fields give
454	        # a total, input-order-independent ordering, so the point itself
455	        # is never compared.
456	        h0 = heuristic(start)
457	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
458	        came_from = {}
459	        g_score = {start: 0}
460	        closed = set()
461	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
462	    else:
463	        open_heap = state["open"]
464	        came_from = state["came_from"]
465	        g_score = state["g_score"]
466	        closed = state["closed"]
467	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
468	    budget_stop = False
469	
470	    while open_heap:
471	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
472	        current = entry[4]
473	        if current in closed:
474	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
475	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:
476	            # A live candidate remains but the budget is spent; close
477	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
478	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
479	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
480	            # snapshot it is pushed back: the checkpoint must hold every
481	            # still-live candidate for the search to resume exactly.
482	            budget_stop = True
483	            if snapshot:
484	                heapq.heappush(open_heap, entry)
485	            break
486	        closed.add(current)
487	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
488	            expanded_nodes.append(current)
489	        if current == goal:
490	            path = [current]
491	            while path[-1] in came_from:
492	                path.append(came_from[path[-1]])
493	            path.reverse()
494	            result = {
495	                "path": path,
496	                "cost": g_score[current],
497	                "expanded": len(closed),
498	            }
499	            if max_expanded is not None:
500	                result["status"] = "found"
501	            if trace:
502	                result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
503	            return result
504	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
505	            nxt = (current[0] + dx, current[1] + dy)
506	            if not (0 <= nxt[0] < width and 0 <= nxt[1] < height):
507	                continue
508	            if nxt in obstacles:
509	                continue
510	            new_g = g_score[current] + step_cost(nxt)
511	            if new_g < g_score.get(nxt, float("inf")):
512	                g_score[nxt] = new_g
513	                came_from[nxt] = current
514	                h = heuristic(nxt)
515	                heapq.heappush(
516	                    open_heap, (new_g + h, h, nxt[0], nxt[1], nxt)
517	                )
518	    result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": len(closed)}
519	    if max_expanded is not None:
520	        result["status"] = (
521	            "budget_exhausted" if budget_stop else "unreachable"
522	        )
523	    if trace:
524	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
525	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
526	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
527	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, None,
528	            len(closed), expanded_nodes,
529	            _static_snapshot_state(open_heap, came_from, g_score, closed),
530	        )
531	    return result

534	def _search_dynamic(width, height, obstacles, frames, start, goal, costs,
535	                    trace, max_expanded, snapshot=False, state=None):
536	    """History-sensitive time-expanded A*.
537	
538	    Frame ``t`` constrains the cell occupied at path index ``t``; frames
539	    past the last one reuse the last frame. Waiting in place and repeated
540	    coordinates are forbidden, so whether a candidate route can be
541	    extended depends on the exact sequence of cells it already visited:
542	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories
543	    are distinct states and neither may prune the other (the route with
544	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
545	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
546	    search is a best-first traversal of the feasible route tree. Goal
547	    closings are collected until the heap's smallest f exceeds the best
548	    goal cost, after which the minimum-cost goal tie-break is settled by
549	    the fixed f, h, x, y, t priority and then the complete path's
550	    lexicographic order. With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally
551	    returns a checkpoint of the complete route-tree state; ``state``
552	    carries such a snapshot back in for ``resume``.
553	    """
554	
555	    def heuristic(point):
556	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
557	
558	    def step_cost(point):
559	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
560	        if costs is None:
561	            return 1
562	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
563	
564	    last_frame = len(frames) - 1
565	
566	    def frame_cells(t):
567	        return frames[t] if t <= last_frame else frames[last_frame]
568	
569	    # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, t, g, path, seen): f/h/x/y/t give the
570	    # fixed numeric priority and candidates still tied are ordered by the
571	    # complete coordinate path lexicographically, so ordering never depends
572	    # on obstacle sets, in-frame coordinate order, or traversal order. The
573	    # frozenset ``seen`` mirrors ``path`` for an O(1) repeat check and is
574	    # never compared (distinct histories always differ in ``path``).
575	    if state is None:
576	        h0 = heuristic(start)
577	        start_path = (start,)
578	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], 0, 0, start_path,
579	                      frozenset(start_path))]
580	        closed_count = 0
581	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
582	        # Best goal closing seen so far, keyed exactly as the tie-break
583	        # specializes at the goal: (g, t, path) (there f == g, h == 0 and
584	        # (x, y) is fixed). Closing a goal does not stop the search
585	        # immediately: an equally cheap route whose chain runs through
586	        # higher-h nodes might still be undeveloped. Since each move costs
587	        # at least 1 and the Manhattan h changes by at most 1 per move,
588	        # f = g + h never decreases along a route; once the smallest f on
589	        # the heap exceeds the best goal cost, no route of that cost (or
590	        # less) can remain undiscovered.
591	        best_key = None
592	    else:
593	        open_heap = state["open"]
594	        closed_count = state["closed_count"]
595	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
596	        best_key = state["best_key"]
597	    budget_stop = False
598	
599	    while open_heap:
600	        if best_key is not None and open_heap[0][0] > best_key[0]:
601	            break
602	        if max_expanded is not None and closed_count >= max_expanded:
603	            # Live route candidates remain but the budget is spent; close
604	            # nothing more. A goal already closed still wins below.
605	            budget_stop = True
606	            break
607	        _, _, x, y, t, g, path, seen = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
608	        closed_count += 1  # every popped route node closes exactly once
609	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
610	            # Histories reaching the same (x, y, t) each record a triple,
611	            # in the order their route nodes are actually closed.
612	            expanded_nodes.append((x, y, t))
613	        if (x, y) == goal:
614	            goal_key = (g, t, path)
615	            if best_key is None or goal_key < best_key:
616	                best_key = goal_key
617	            continue  # routes end at the goal; never expanded past it
618	        next_t = t + 1
619	        frame = frame_cells(next_t)
620	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
621	            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
622	            if not (0 <= nx < width and 0 <= ny < height):
623	                continue
624	            nxt = (nx, ny)
625	            if nxt in obstacles or nxt in frame or nxt in seen:
626	                continue  # static obstacle, timed obstacle, or revisit
627	            new_g = g + step_cost(nxt)
628	            new_path = path + (nxt,)
629	            h = heuristic(nxt)
630	            heapq.heappush(
631	                open_heap,
632	                (new_g + h, h, nx, ny, next_t, new_g, new_path,
633	                 seen | {nxt}),
634	            )
635	    if best_key is None:
636	        result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": closed_count}
637	        if max_expanded is not None:
638	            result["status"] = (
639	                "budget_exhausted" if budget_stop else "unreachable"
640	            )
641	    else:
642	        best_g, _, best_path = best_key
643	        result = {
644	            "path": list(best_path),
645	            "cost": best_g,
646	            "expanded": closed_count,
647	        }
648	        if max_expanded is not None:
649	            result["status"] = "found"
650	    if trace:
651	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
652	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
653	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
654	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, frames,
655	            closed_count, expanded_nodes,
656	            _tree_snapshot_state(open_heap, best_key, "plan"),
657	        )
658	    return result

795	def _snapshot_checkpoint(planner, width, height, obstacles, start, endpoints,
796	                         costs, frames, closed_count, expanded_nodes, state):
797	    # The checkpoint is built from JSON-native values only (ints, strings,
798	    # lists, dicts, ``None``) in one fixed key order, and every list
799	    # derived from a set is sorted, so neither set iteration order, goal
800	    # order nor in-frame coordinate order can influence the result.
801	    checkpoint = {
802	        "version": _SNAPSHOT_VERSION,
803	        "planner": planner,
804	        "width": width,
805	        "height": height,
806	        "blocked": [[cell[0], cell[1]] for cell in sorted(obstacles)],
807	        "start": [start[0], start[1]],
808	    }
809	    if planner == "plan":
810	        checkpoint["goal"] = [endpoints[0], endpoints[1]]
811	    else:
812	        checkpoint["goals"] = [[goal[0], goal[1]] for goal in endpoints]
813	    checkpoint["costs"] = (
814	        [list(row) for row in costs] if costs is not None else None
815	    )
816	    checkpoint["dynamic_blocked"] = (
817	        [[[cell[0], cell[1]] for cell in sorted(frame)]
818	         for frame in frames]
819	        if frames is not None else None
820	    )
821	    checkpoint["closed"] = closed_count
822	    checkpoint["trace"] = [list(entry) for entry in expanded_nodes]
823	    checkpoint["state"] = state

829	    # it verbatim keeps the exact future pop order), the route
830	    # reconstruction links, the best-known costs and the closed set.

832	        "open": [[entry[0], entry[1], entry[2], entry[3]]
833	                 for entry in open_heap],
834	        "came_from": [
835	            [[point[0], point[1]], [parent[0], parent[1]]]
836	            for point, parent in sorted(came_from.items())
837	        ],
838	        "g_score": [
839	            [[point[0], point[1]], g]
840	            for point, g in sorted(g_score.items())
841	        ],

846	def _tree_snapshot_state(open_heap, best_key, planner):
847	    # The complete route-tree state: every live candidate with its full
848	    # coordinate history (the ``seen`` frozenset is derived from the path
849	    # on restore) plus the best goal closing recorded so far, keyed as
850	    # (g, t, path) for ``plan`` and (g, (x, y), path) for ``plan_any``.
851	    if best_key is None:
852	        best = None
853	    else:
854	        best_g, best_tie, best_path = best_key
855	        best = [
856	            best_g,
857	            [best_tie[0], best_tie[1]] if planner == "plan_any" else best_tie,
858	            [[point[0], point[1]] for point in best_path],
859	        ]
860	    return {
861	        "open": [
862	            [f, h, x, y, t, g, [[point[0], point[1]] for point in path]]
863	            for f, h, x, y, t, g, path, _seen in open_heap
864	        ],
865	        "best": best,
866	    }
